clue.text: Vital to take doctor and soldiers across the Atlantic

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
soldiers are men, the rank and file
taken as written
seen from Britain, across the Atlantic lies the US

explanation.surface: An urgent call for a doctor and troops to be flown over to America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' is only a link here; 'across the Atlantic' looks like a journey but just names the country over the ocean from Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vital is of great consequence, a synonym for highly significant.

clue.text: Architect removing King's coat.

indicators.note: one letter is taken away from the architect's name

parts.note: Charles Rennie Mackintosh was a Scottish architect and designer
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: An architect takes the king's coat off him.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking K from the architect's name leaves the spelling of the raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A macintosh is a waterproof raincoat, named after its inventor Charles Macintosh.

clue.text: Fight to get East from road off motorway

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

indicators.note: the compass letter is taken away from the slip-road word

parts.note: an exit is a road leading off

explanation.surface: A driver argues over leaving the motorway eastbound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get East from' takes E out of EXIT, leaving XIT. The M1 is a British motorway, written MI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To mix it is an informal idiom for to brawl or start trouble.

clue.text: The Pony Express's first new recruit

indicators.note: something new is made over, so the letters are rearranged
only the opening letter of the word Express is taken

explanation.surface: The Pony Express takes on a fresh rider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges THE PONY into NEOPHYT, and E, the first letter of 'Express's', ends the answer. The Pony Express was a 19th-century US mail service.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a beginner or novice, someone newly enrolled.

clue.text: University pair producing neat game

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so one beast is an ox
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Two universities put on a tidy match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like tidy, but it is an old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxbridge is the collective name for Oxford and Cambridge universities.

clue.text: Head's fine for 4 students

explanation.surface: The principal fines students at the old universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Sconce is an old jocular word for the skull, and at Oxford it was a penalty imposed on undergraduates.

clue.text: Father William's capital fruit

parts.note: papa is a child's word for father

indicators.note: a capital letter is the initial, so only the first letter of the name is used

explanation.surface: Dad tells young William that a certain fruit is splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like praise ('capital fruit!'), but it asks for William's capital letter, W.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaw (pawpaw) is a tropical fruit, another name for papaya.

clue.text: Depart in order to get explosive device

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Leave so as to obtain a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges DEPART; 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A petard was a small bomb for blowing open gates, as in hoist with one's own petard.

clue.text: Chose college, say, for magazine

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: chose is picked, and Oriel is an Oxford college

explanation.surface: Picking a college, for example, for a periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'picked Oriel' sounds like the answer; Oriel is an Oxford college.
explanation.definitionFit: A pictorial is an illustrated periodical, one carrying many pictures.

clue.text: Reliable sources for a historian

explanation.surface: Trustworthy references for a history scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: Springs are dependable sources of water, and H. G. Wells wrote The Outline of History.

clue.text: One over the eight? Search for dandy

parts.note: the cox sits in charge of the eight rowers in a racing boat
to comb is to search thoroughly

explanation.surface: Someone a drink past sober is seeking a fop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is British slang for slightly drunk, but here it is the cox steering a rowing eight.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxcomb is a vain, showy man, an old word for a fop.

clue.text: Sort of illusion that's shattered in 27

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into pieces, so the letters of the referenced entry are rearranged

parts.note: the entry at 27 across is the mine word, a pit for coal

explanation.surface: A trick of the eye is smashed inside a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' rearranges the letters of 27 across, COALPIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical illusion is a trick played on the eye, a common kind of visual deception.

clue.text: Make a record score

explanation.surface: Set a new best mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To notch is to cut a mark recording a tally, and a notch is a nick or score cut into wood.

clue.text: Run into debt — without interest.

parts.note: to incur a cost is to run into it
IOUs are written promises to pay, acknowledgements of debt

explanation.surface: Running up debts with no interest charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without interest' looks like a loan term, but means lacking curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone incurious shows no curiosity, lacking any wish to know more.

clue.text: Non-playing coach attached to cricket side

indicators.note: one piece is joined on after the other, so the coach word follows the side word

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
a stage is a stagecoach

explanation.surface: A coach who does not play is tied to a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the leg side. 'Side' suggests a team, and 'coach' a trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor offstage is out of view and not performing at that moment.

clue.text: Brave clergy used to clean up 22.

parts.note: to brave a danger is to face it
the cloth is a collective term for the clergy

explanation.surface: Courageous clerics are employed to tidy things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 down is KISSER, slang for the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A flannel for washing the face, a small towel used to wipe the mouth and cheeks.

clue.text: Top man essential on board

explanation.surface: The leader is vital to the company board.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is the top man of a realm, and the chess piece of that name must be kept on the board.

clue.text: Elmer omits nothing in courageous behaviour

annotationWithheld.why: Elmer omits nothing in courageous behaviour: GANTRY (Elmer Gantry) around ALL, but ALL and the insertion both come from 'omits nothing', a phrase doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Elmer omits nothing in courageous behaviour

clue.text: Matter of little importance writing under a page

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece below comes after, so the writing follows the page

parts.note: an article is a piece of writing in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A trivial matter: a piece written beneath a page.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'under' puts ARTICLE after P; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle is a tiny speck of matter, something minute and insignificant.

clue.text: Recoil. from stern whipping

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship
a lash is a stroke of the whip

explanation.surface: Flinching from a beating on the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' looks like severe, but it is the rear of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlash is a recoil or sharp reaction, as in machinery or public opinion.

clue.text: Joint production on the Rhine

explanation.surface: A combined show staged by the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: The hock is a joint in an animal's hind leg; it is also a German white wine from the Rhineland.

clue.text: Corresponding without ever meeting

explanation.surface: Pen pals who write to each other but never meet.
explanation.definitionFit: Matching things run side by side, and lines of this kind never meet however far extended.

clue.text: Sort of Iron Age bird

parts.note: pig iron is crude iron from a blast furnace
an eon is an age, a vast period

explanation.surface: A bird from the Iron Age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Age' looks like the historical period, but splits into pig iron and an eon.
explanation.definitionFit: The pigeon is a common bird, a dove.

clue.text: Mouth 'expression of love to the king

parts.note: a kiss expresses affection
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A mouth shows love to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. ER is usually the Queen, but Edward VII also signed ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Kisser is slang for the mouth or face.

clue.text: This vicar could be a record holder

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged to form something else

explanation.surface: Perhaps the parish priest keeps the records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges THIS VICAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps archives looks after historical records and documents.

clue.text: Produce new lines for As You Like It?

explanation.surface: Rewriting lines for a Shakespeare comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise is to make up words on the spot, and the Latin ad libitum means at one's pleasure.

clue.text: A bit of Greek, apparently

indicators.note: only part of the words Greek and apparently is taken, their last letter and first four running together

explanation.surface: Someone seems to know a little Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds it: the letters run from the end of 'Greek' into 'apparently', and a letter of the Greek alphabet is a bit of Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Kappa is the tenth letter of the Greek alphabet, a small piece of that language's writing.

clue.text: Enliven wise-sounding naval administrator

parts.note: to pep up is to enliven

indicators.note: sounding signals the word is spoken, giving letters that sound like it

parts.note: wise said aloud sounds like the letter Y twice, Y's

explanation.surface: Liven up a knowing-sounding official of the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Pepys, the diarist, was a senior administrator at the Navy Board.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys ran the Admiralty office as Secretary, a navy official.

clue.text: Partner of majority shareholder loses in crash

indicators.note: a crash wrecks things, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A company's main shareholder's spouse loses money in a stock crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' rearranges LOSES IN. The 'lion's share' is the biggest part, so the lion is the majority shareholder.
explanation.definitionFit: A lion's mate is the female lion, playing on the idiom lion's share for the largest portion.

clue.text: A record in company — it's mine

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record
the word it, with the 's standing for is as a link

explanation.surface: A firm owns a record label and claims the disc as its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like a possessive, but it is a pit dug for coal.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal pit is a coal mine, a colliery.

clue.text: Hard-hearted American head's seen Irish author

indicators.note: a heart sits in the middle, so the hard letter goes inside the head word

parts.note: bean is American slang for the head
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A tough US chief meets an Irish writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard-hearted' reads as callous, but it means H at the heart of BEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Brendan Behan was an Irish playwright and novelist, author of Borstal Boy.

clue.text: Drink port 'in front of carriage

indicators.note: one piece is placed before the next, so the town comes first

parts.note: Rye is one of the Cinque Ports on England's south coast
a whisky (or whiskey) is an old light two-wheeled carriage

explanation.surface: Someone drinks port before stepping into the coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the fortified wine, but it is the harbour town of Rye in Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye whisky is a spirit distilled from rye grain, a strong drink.
